messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point numbers have limited precision, meaning not every real number can be represented exactly. This imprecision leads to rounding errors during floating-point addition, and the order in which operations are performed can affect these rounding errors. Consequently, (a + b) + c may yield a slightly different result than a + (b + c) due to the accumulation of these rounding discrepancies, demonstrating a lack of associativity.

Floating-point numbers have limited precision, meaning not every real number can be represented exactly. This imprecision leads to rounding errors during floating-point addition, and the order in which operations are performed can affect *which* numbers are rounded. Consequently, (a + b) + c may yield a slightly different result than a + (b + c) due to these accumulated rounding differences, breaking the associative property.
